messages:
nora: Hey team — putting together a tiny onboarding sample for Vercel Edge Functions and hit a puzzling runtime error. Need advice on dual-package publishing.
liam: paste the error and how you import it.
nora: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'then')` during Client initialization. Only happens when deployed to edge; local node works fine. Import is `import { Client } from 'redwood-sdk'` (using our SDK).
anya: that smells like CJS code sneaking into an ESM runtime. Which entrypoint did Vercel resolve?
nora: our package.json exports: "\." : { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs" } and `main` -> `dist/cjs/index.cjs`.
liam: Vercel/Edge bundlers sometimes prefer `main` or rewrite imports. Also if the ESM build contains any `require()` calls, it can blow up in workers.
anya: do we have any runtime-detect code that `require()`s node polyfills? I remember an auth helper that conditionally loads `node:http`/`node-fetch` for Node.
nora: yep — the auth/retry helper tries `const fetch = globalThis.fetch || require('node-fetch')` in source and build step left a `require('node-fetch')` in the esm artifact.
liam: aha. So two problems: publishing metadata + build hygiene. Suggestions: 1) make the esm output strictly ESM (no `require`/`module.exports`) 2) add "browser": "./dist/esm/index.mjs" to exports to bias bundlers toward ESM for browser/edge 3) add an explicit "./types": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" } export to make TS resolution deterministic.
anya: also, we have divergent auth/retry implementations — the cjs build pulls in the legacy retry wrapper while esm uses fetch-based retries. That explains parity flakiness in integ tests. We should have a single runtime-agnostic auth module compiled into both bundles.
nora: agreed. I can refactor auth/retry into `src/runtime/auth.ts` that avoids node-only calls and uses small runtime adapters imported at entrypoints.
liam: CI fixes: add a short lint that greps `dist/esm` for `require(` and `module.exports` and fails the job. Add a `tsc --traceResolution` check against a tiny sample consumer to verify types resolution. Also add a resolver-smoke test that simulates node import, webpack, and an edge bundler so we catch export resolution regressions.
anya: tradeoffs: temporarily setting `main` -> esm reduces edge fallout but will break some CJS `require()` users. We could ship a patch and note it in the changelog, but prefer the build + exports fixes first.
nora: I'll add a minimal Vercel worker repro to sample-apps and a note in onboarding docs to check your bundler config (ensure ESM entry is preferred).
liam: one more: for downstream bundlers that follow `package.main` even for ESM (ugh), adding "exports.\".\".browser" helps, and some bundlers respect `module` and `browser` fields. So include "module": "dist/esm/index.mjs" and `browser` in package.json too.
anya: and for types: some editors still pick up `dist/cjs/index.d.ts` if exports map ambiguous. The explicit `./types` export + `types` at root should stabilize IDEs. Add a CI job that runs `npm pack` and then node -p "require('module').createRequire('./node_modules/your-test/').resolve('redwood-sdk')" style resolution tests.
ci-bot: ci/checks — added esm-scan + tsc-resolution + resolver-smoke jobs to the PR pipeline (PR #789).
build-bot: build/artifacts — sample-app worker repro added in branch `nora/edge-repro`.
liam: great. After PR lands, let's run canary on the sample app and reach out to the customer. Also add a short note in the DX cookbook about dual-publish pitfalls (auth shims, types resolution, exports map).
nora: will do a follow-up PR that factors auth and adds the lint. thanks all :thumbsup:
